roster.name: Mega Charizard Y
roster.rationale: Mega Charizard Y is the premier sun setter and an immediate offensive nuclear threat with 159 SpA Drought-boosted Heat Waves. It defines an entire archetype — sun — which gives the draft a clear strategic identity from pick one. At 20 points it's the maximum I can spend while leaving exactly 80 for the remaining 9 picks, but the return is a weather-controlling, speed-tier-defining (100 base) special sweeper that doubles as a win condition and a team builder's compass.

roster.name: Venusaur
roster.rationale: The classic Chlorophyll partner for Zard Y sun. Venusaur doubles its speed under Drought, threatens Water and Rock types with Grass STAB, and brings Sleep Powder for disruption plus Weather Ball for flexible coverage. At 13 points it's excellent value and locks in the core win condition before anyone can deny it.

roster.name: Krookodile
roster.rationale: Krookodile (9) gives the sun core exactly what it needs: Ground STAB to crush Rock/Electric switch-ins aimed at Zard Y, Intimidate to cycle with switches and blunt physical attackers like Mega Gengar, and a Dark typing that blanks Farigiraf's Psychic STAB. At 92 Speed it outspeeds most defensive mons, and Taunt access gives me a Trick Room counter without spending a dedicated slot. At 9 points it leaves 58 for 7 picks (8.3 avg).

roster.name: Sinistcha
roster.rationale: Sinistcha (18) is the ideal rain pivot for a sun squad: Grass/Ghost resists Water and threatens Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha, while Heatproof neutralises its Fire weakness—crucial when Grok's rain is the biggest structural threat. Hospitality provides passive ally healing on switch-in, and the Ghost typing gives an extra Shadow Tag escape and Fake Out immunity. At 18 pts it leaves 40 for 6 picks, and with back-to-back 16–17 I can lock in a second piece immediately.

roster.name: Sableye
roster.rationale: Sableye (14) gives Prankster Quash — the best speed control that works regardless of weather, crucial since my Chlorophyll mode loses to Grok's rain. Will-O-Wisp cripples physical threats like Mega Metagross, Mega Swampert, and Kingambit. Its Dark/Ghost typing is only Fairy-weak and slots neatly alongside Sinistcha without type overlap issues. At 14 pts it leaves 26 for 5 picks (5.2 avg), keeping budget options viable.

roster.name: Hawlucha
roster.rationale: Hawlucha (7) is the ideal physical attacker for this slot: it functions independently of sun, Unburden doubles its speed after item consumption to pair with Sableye's Quash for layered speed control, and Fighting/Flying coverage smashes Kingambit, Steel-types, and Dark-types that threaten the roster. At only 7 points it preserves budget flexibility, leaving 19 points for the final four picks.

roster.name: Hydreigon
roster.rationale: Hydreigon (14) gives me a 125 SpA Levitate special attacker that doesn't rely on sun, with Dark/Dragon typing that resists Ghost and Dark (key into Mega Gengar) and provides crucial Ground immunity to switch in beside Zard Y. Dark Pulse, Draco Meteor, Earth Power, and Flash Cannon offer near-unresisted coverage into the whole field. At 14 points it leaves 5 for the last 3 picks, which is tight but workable with a 2+2+1 budget path.

roster.name: Morpeko
roster.rationale: Morpeko (2) is the most snipable of my shoestring targets: a fast Electric/Dark pivot with Aura Wheel that gives me crucial Electric coverage and a speedy revenge-killer. Spending 2 here leaves me exactly 3 points for the final two picks, which maps perfectly to Slurpuff (2) + Pikachu (1) to round out Fairy and Lightning Rod support.

roster.name: Slurpuff
roster.rationale: Slurpuff (2 pts) fills the missing Fairy type on the roster and brings Unburden for potential speed-swing plays, plus Sweet Veil as a niche sleep immunity option. It leaves exactly 1 point for Pikachu as the final pick, completing the Lightning Rod support for Zard Y while adding Electric redundancy alongside Morpeko. Slurpuff and Pikachu are both still available, and no other coach can snipe both Fairy and Lightning Rod in one pick.

roster.name: Pikachu
roster.rationale: Pikachu (1) is available as planned and brings Lightning Rod to protect Zard Y, Hawlucha, and Slurpuff from Electric attacks — critical against Terra's Rotom-Wash and Moonshot's Rotom-Mow. It also offers Fake Out pressure, Nuzzle speed control, and Volt Switch pivoting, with Light Ball giving it surprising offensive bite despite its frailty. Manectric (1) is the fallback with better bulk and SpA, but Pikachu's support movepool and Fake Out edge out the competition for this sun team's final slot.

roster.name: Archaludon
roster.rationale: Archaludon at 19 is the premier non-Mega pick left: elite Steel/Dragon bulk with Stamina for free Defense boosts, Body Press/Electro Shot/Flash Cannon coverage, and Sturdy/Stalwart options that anchor both offense and defense. With Mega Charizard Y already gone, this gives me a weather-agnostic core piece that pairs into sun, rain, or sand later without locking me into a fragile glass-cannon start. Spending 19 leaves 81 for nine more picks—plenty for speed control, Intimidate, and a Mega of my own.

roster.name: Pelipper
roster.rationale: Archaludon thrives with rain enabling instant Electro Shot + Stamina Body Press bulk, and Pelipper is the premier Drizzle setter still available at 18 while providing Tailwind/Hurricane utility. This locks a strong weather core early before rain pieces get sniped, leaving 63 points for a Mega (Metagross/Dragonite/Swampert tier), Intimidate, and speed control. Avoids overpaying on contested offense like Sneasler/Basculegion while opponents locked sun, Shadow Tag, and Prankster.

roster.name: Mega Swampert
roster.rationale: Mega Swampert perfectly completes the rain core with Pelipper Drizzle enabling Swift Swim + STAB Water/Ground coverage that pairs excellently with Archaludon's Electro Shot and Steel/Dragon bulk. At 15 it secures a premium Mega without overspending while leaving room for Intimidate, Prankster, and Ghost answers. Contested high-value Megas and rain pieces will go fast in the next four picks before my turn.

roster.name: Grimmsnarl
roster.rationale: Grimmsnarl is the premier remaining Prankster for Thunder Wave/screens/Spirit Break support that pairs perfectly with our locked rain core and is highly contested at 16. It fills the speed control and disruption role from the prior plan without overspending, leaving 32 points for 6 picks. Intimidate and Gholdengo remain accessible next while denying opponents a key tool.

roster.name: Gholdengo
roster.rationale: Gholdengo at 16 is the premier secondary rain cleaner and generalist: Good as Gold shuts down status/Prankster, Steel/Ghost walls common threats, and it pairs perfectly with Pelipper rain + Archaludon/Swampert offense without needing weather itself. Leaves 16 points for 5 picks (still room for Hisuian Arcanine Intimidate + Aegislash/Annihilape Ghost answer + Maushold/Tsareena flex while hitting ~3 avg). Basculegion 19 is tempting for pure Swift Swim but overspends and leaves the roster thinner on answers.

roster.name: Gyarados
roster.rationale: Gyarados at 11 fits the max-12 budget and supplies the missing Intimidate support that rain cores desperately want, while adding a strong physical Water/Flying attacker that synergizes with Pelipper rain and can run Moxie, Taunt, or dual dance sets. Azumarill/Palafin are tempting rain abusers but leave us without Intimidate against the many physical threats already drafted (Kingambit, Incineroar, Metagross, Excadrill). Leaves 5 points for four flexible fillers.

roster.name: Qwilfish
roster.rationale: Qwilfish at 2pts perfectly fits the rain core with Swift Swim + Intimidate stacking on Gyarados, adding Water/Poison coverage and utility (spikes/taunt/destiny bond) while answering grass threats. Leaves exactly 3pts for the final three fillers as required. Highest-value available piece under the hard 2pt cap that advances speed control and defensive modes.

roster.name: Forretress
roster.rationale: Forretress is the clearest 1pt defensive backbone left that fits the rain core: Sturdy + hazards (Rocks/Spikes synergy with Qwilfish), Body Press bulk, and a reliable switch-in vs Fairy/Flying/Fire pressure the field still has. It rounds the roster without competing for Mega or rain roles while leaving exactly 2pts for the final two 1s. Priority options like Absol are secondary once the wall slot is secured.

roster.name: Absol
roster.rationale: Absol is the best remaining 1pt for physical priority (Sucker Punch) and Dark coverage to complement rain offense, Gholdengo, and Archaludon while adding Super Luck/Justified options. It fills the speed/priority gap without overlapping roles; remaining 1pt will round bulk/utility next.

roster.name: Avalugg
roster.rationale: Avalugg provides the best remaining 1pt defensive glue as a massive physical wall with Ice typing that complements the rain core, checking Dragons, Flyings, and Grounds while offering reliable bulk and utility like Recover/Body Press. It rounds out the roster without overlapping roles already covered by Archaludon, Forretress, Gholdengo, and Grimmsnarl.

roster.name: Mega Gengar
roster.rationale: Mega Gengar is the most format-warping piece left on the board: Shadow Tag is a unique, non-replaceable mechanic in a Bo3 open-teamsheet league, letting me trap and remove a problem support or set up a partner with impunity. Its 170 SpA / 130 Spe stat line is an elite special nuke on top of the trapping, and at 18 points I keep 82 for 9 picks, which comfortably funds speed control and a defensive backbone later. Speed control and Intimidate have multiple replacements on this board; Shadow Tag has zero, so I secure it now before coach 4's double pick.

roster.name: Incineroar
roster.rationale: Coach 4 grabbed Whimsicott and Farigiraf instead, so Incineroar survives to me exactly as planned — it's the best glue in the pool and covers three of Mega Gengar's four weaknesses (immune Psychic, resists Dark/Ghost) while Intimidate and Fake Out buy the turns Shadow Tag needs to convert traps into KOs. Snarl also soft-checks Mega Charizard Y, and Knock Off/Darkest Lariat pressures the Ghost- and Psychic-types that scare Gengar. At 18 it fits the 20-point cap, leaving 64 points for 8 picks.

roster.name: Kingambit
roster.rationale: Kingambit survived the four picks before me and it's my top target: Dark/Steel resists or is immune to all of Mega Gengar's weaknesses (Ghost, Dark, Psychic), giving my Shadow Tag trapper a safe partner, while Sucker Punch, Kowtow Cleave, and Defiant/Supreme Overlord make it a genuine breaker that also matches up well into Archaludon and any Trick Room builds Terra might assemble. Krookodile going to DeepSeek removes my cheap fallback, so I can't risk Kingambit being taken by Grok's or Terra's slow teams at 12-15. At 17 points I stay on budget with 47 left for 7 picks, enough for speed control and an anti-rain piece.

roster.name: Noivern
roster.rationale: Noivern at 9 is my cheapest one-slot fix for two structural problems: Tailwind speed control and a Ground immunity for a roster (Gengar/Incineroar/Kingambit) that is triple Ground-weak into DeepSeek's Krookodile and any EQ spam. Its Flying/Dragon typing also resists Fire and 4x-resists Grass, making it a natural pivot into DeepSeek's Zard Y + Chlorophyll Venusaur sun mode, and Infiltrator lets its damage bypass screens/Subs. Taking it now rather than Rotom-Mow because Grok (rain) won't want it while speed-control pieces are scarcer board-wide.

roster.name: Rotom-Mow
roster.rationale: Rotom-Mow (10) is my #1 priority and it survived: its STABs hit Grok's rain core 4x on both sides (Thunderbolt vs Pelipper, Leaf Storm vs Mega Swampert), Levitate blanks Earthquake while resisting Water/Electric/Steel, so it walls huge chunks of Grok's roster (Archaludon, Gholdengo too) and also beats Terra's Rotom-Wash. Grok can't afford a Swift Swim sweeper anymore (16 pts left) and Terra already owns Rotom-Wash, but at 10 points this is too central to my anti-rain plan to risk. Leaves 28 points for 5 picks, right on budget.

roster.name: Hatterene
roster.rationale: Terra's double pick locked in a Tailwind team (Whimsicott + Excadrill + Mega Metagross), and Grok's rain is also fast, so a Trick Room mode is now essential. Hatterene is my ideal setter: 29 Speed, Magic Bounce bounces Taunt/Thunder Wave from DeepSeek's Sableye and Grok's Grimmsnarl, and it flips Kingambit/Incineroar into slow-mode threats. DeepSeek picks twice before my next turn and could pair Hatterene with Sinistcha, so I take it now — 9 points leaves exactly 19 for my planned finish of Lycanroc-Dusk + Garganacl + Gliscor + Skarmory.

roster.name: Lycanroc-Dusk
roster.rationale: Locking in my anti-DeepSeek insurance: Tough Claws Accelerock (confirmed +1 priority) is a clean revenge kill on Mega Charizard Y even through sun — the damage tool omits Tough Claws and still shows a possible OHKO — and it gives my roster the Rock offense it currently lacks into Fire/Flying and Volcarona-style threats. Only Terra could afford to poach it, and it doesn't fit their Metagross/Excadrill structure, whereas Garganacl has real poach risk but also viable fallbacks (Swampert/Rhyperior). At 8 points this keeps my exact 8+5+3+3 = 19 budget intact.

roster.name: Garganacl
roster.rationale: Garganacl is my keystone anti-DeepSeek piece and it's still on the board: pure Rock resists both Mega Charizard Y STABs (Fire and Flying 0.5x each), and Wide Guard (+3 priority) blanks Heat Wave in sun, Rock Slide, Earthquake, and Grok's Make It Rain/Muddy Water. Purifying Salt makes it immune to Sinistcha/Sableye burn and sleep while halving Gholdengo Shadow Ball, and its 35 Speed lets it double as a Trick Room attacker with Salt Cure/Recover/Body Press under Hatterene. I'm taking it now because DeepSeek (5 pts) picks twice at 32/33 before my next turn and could poach it, while Grok (3 pts) can't afford it.

roster.name: Gliscor
roster.rationale: Four of my eight are Ground-weak (Gengar, Incineroar, Kingambit, Garganacl) and Terra's Excadrill plus DeepSeek's Krookodile exploit that, so Gliscor gives me a third Ground immunity that also walls and EQs Excadrill back. Poison Heal + Toxic chip pairs perfectly with Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag trapping, and at 3 points it leaves exactly 3 for Skarmory at 38. Gliscor is unpoachable: Terra (36/37) has only 2 points for two picks and Grok/DeepSeek (39/40) have 1 each, so no one left can afford a 3-cost before my final pick.

roster.name: Skarmory
roster.rationale: Skarmory is guaranteed available — DeepSeek and Grok can only afford 1-costs and Terra's roster is full — so I lock in my planned final piece for exactly 3 points and finish at 100/100 spent. It gives me a Sturdy Steel/Flying physical wall and a fourth Ground immunity, directly answering Terra's Excadrill and Mega Metagross cores while phazing Trick Room and setup with Whirlwind. Spikes/Stealth Rock chip also synergizes with Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag traps, forcing damaged switches Gengar can pick off.

Poison Heal + Toxic chip pairs perfectly with Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag trapping, and at 3 points it leaves exactly 3 for Skarmory at 38. Gliscor is unpoachable: Terra (36/37) has only 2 points for two picks and Grok/DeepSeek (39/40) have 1 each, so no one left can afford a 3-cost before my final pick.

draftRoster.name: Skarmory
draftRoster.rationale: Skarmory is guaranteed available — DeepSeek and Grok can only afford 1-costs and Terra's roster is full — so I lock in my planned final piece for exactly 3 points and finish at 100/100 spent. It gives me a Sturdy Steel/Flying physical wall and a fourth Ground immunity, directly answering Terra's Excadrill and Mega Metagross cores while phazing Trick Room and setup with Whirlwind. Spikes/Stealth Rock chip also synergizes with Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag traps, forcing damaged switches Gengar can pick off.

roster.name: Whimsicott
roster.rationale: Whimsicott is the board’s most reliable universal speed-control piece and gives this roster immediate access to Prankster Tailwind, Encore, Taunt, and weather disruption. Its flexibility will support either a fast offensive shell or a slower anti-Trick Room mode while remaining useful into all three early opposing cores.

roster.name: Farigiraf
roster.rationale: Farigiraf gives the roster an excellent second speed mode with Trick Room while Armor Tail protects Whimsicott and slower partners from priority disruption. Its Normal typing also makes it immune to Mega Gengar’s Ghost STAB, and its bulky support profile is valuable into the aggressive Charizard Y / Archaludon cores already drafted.

roster.name: Mega Metagross
roster.rationale: Mega Metagross is an exceptional 17-point primary Mega that gives the roster immediate Steel-type resistance, premium physical pressure, and a fast Tailwind mode beside Whimsicott. Its Psychic typing also pressures the Fighting-types that naturally target our future Steel/Dark pivots, while Farigiraf blocks priority attempts to revenge it.

roster.name: Rotom-Wash
roster.rationale: Rotom-Wash is the cleanest role-compression pick: it pressures Mega Charizard Y, Pelipper, Mega Swampert, and Archaludon while providing a Ground immunity and flexible pivoting. It gives the roster a valuable rain matchup piece without committing to weather, and its defensive profile pairs well with both Mega Metagross and Farigiraf.

roster.name: Arcanine
roster.rationale: Arcanine is the efficient Intimidate pivot this roster needs, with Snarl, Will-O-Wisp, speed control pressure, and Fire coverage to support Mega Metagross into Steel-heavy boards. It is especially valuable into Moonshot’s physical Dark/Steel core and helps soften Mega Swampert, while Rotom-Wash covers its Ground weakness.

roster.name: Excadrill
roster.rationale: Excadrill gives the roster the immediate Ground-type physical pressure it lacks, while Mold Breaker provides unusually valuable flexibility into opposing Rotom formes and defensive abilities. It threatens Grok’s Gholdengo and Archaludon especially well, fits both Whimsicott Tailwind and Farigiraf Trick Room denial support, and leaves 8 points for four cheap but targeted utility picks.

roster.name: Serperior
roster.rationale: Serperior is the best available ≤5-point addition: Contrary Leaf Storm gives the roster a genuine offensive anti-rain button into Pelipper/Mega Swampert while its 113 base Speed works naturally under Whimsicott Tailwind. It also supplies valuable Water-, Ground-, and Electric-pressure insurance without adding another Mega or competing for the roster’s core items.

roster.name: Altaria
roster.rationale: Altaria is the best one-point role player for this roster because Cloud Nine gives us an on-demand answer to both opposing weather cores: Charizard Y/Venusaur sun and Pelipper/Mega Swampert rain. Its Dragon/Flying typing also supplies a valuable Ground immunity alongside Rotom-W, while it can flex into supportive Tailwind, Haze, Helping Hand, or Perish Song utility depending on matchup.

roster.name: Banette
roster.rationale: Banette is the best 1-point matchup pick because its Ghost typing is immune to Mega Gengar’s Shadow Tag, giving the roster a crucial switch-out option in the Moonshot matchup. It also offers disruptive utility such as Will-O-Wisp, Disable, and Destiny Bond, while preserving the final point for another cheap specialist.

roster.name: Appletun
roster.rationale: Appletun is exceptional 1-point rain insurance: Grass/Dragon resists Water fourfold and Electric, while Thick Fat makes it a far less exploitable Grass slot into Fire/Ice coverage. Its bulky Recover/Apple Acid utility gives the roster a durable answer to Pelipper–Mega Swampert and Rotom-W structures without competing with Serperior’s faster Contrary pressure.

teambuilds.rationale: Lead pressure centers on Prankster Tailwind or disruption from Whimsicott beside Mega Metagross, with Serperior deleting Mega Swampert even through rain. Rotom-Wash punishes Pelipper and Gyarados, while Altaria’s Cloud Nine removes Swift Swim and rain amplification; Arcanine supplies Intimidate, Snarl, and immediate Fire pressure into Gholdengo, Forretress, and Archaludon. Preserve Altaria for rain compositions and use Whimsicott Taunt/Encore aggressively against Grimmsnarl screens and setup.

Cloud Nine Altaria removes Drought’s Fire/Solar Beam/Chlorophyll advantages, making Venusaur manageable and restoring Rotom-Wash’s Water pressure. Jolly Mega Metagross is built to outrun even max-Speed Mega Charizard Y and non-Scarf Hydreigon, while Whimsicott supplies faster Tailwind or Taunt disruption. Armor Tail Farigiraf blocks priority pressure from Sableye, Morpeko, and Pikachu and provides a Trick Room reversal option; Arcanine and Rotom form the bulky anti-special/anti-physical pivot core.

Rain hard-wins the weather war vs Mega Charizard Y and Chlorophyll Venusaur: Drizzle + Damp Rock keeps Water STAB and Swift Swim online while gutting Fire power. Mega Swampert and Archaludon (Electro Shot) are the primary win conditions under rain; Gyarados Intimidate + DD pressures Hawlucha/Hydreigon/Krookodile; Grimmsnarl Prankster screens and Fake Out blunt Unburden and Sableye; Gholdengo Good as Gold ignores status and walls Dark/Ghost while hitting Grass and Flying. Electric answers and Levitate Hydreigon are covered by Ground/Steel/special coverage and speed control.

The core is Tailwind Mega Metagross pressure, with direct OHKO coverage on Mega Gengar, Hatterene, and Kingambit once positioning is established. Armor Tail Farigiraf is the key anti-priority and anti-Shadow Tag pivot: it is immune to Ghost attacks and can Imprison Trick Room, while Banette gives us a trapped-mode answer with Kasib Berry, Shadow Sneak, and Destiny Bond. Rotom-Wash and Arcanine cover Incineroar, Lycanroc, Gliscor, Skarmory, and the opponent’s physical pressure through burn and Intimidate.

Opponent has Cloud Nine Altaria to blank rain, Armor Tail Farigiraf, Prankster Whimsicott, and strong physical threats in Mega Metagross and Excadrill. We still lean on the rain core (Pelipper + Mega Swampert + Archaludon + Gyarados) for Swift Swim pressure and Electro Shot, while Gholdengo provides Good as Gold status immunity and Steel/Ghost coverage that pressures Fairies, Altaria, and Metagross. Grimmsnarl Light Clay screens blunt the physical attackers and give Prankster control into Whimsicott/Farigiraf leads.

Sun vs Rain weather war. Charizard Y resets weather to sun, Venusaur (Chlorophyll) outspeeds and OHKOs Mega Swampert with Giga Drain. Sinistcha redirects with Rage Powder and threatens Swampert with Matcha Gotcha. Krookodile provides Intimidate and Ground coverage into Archaludon/Gholdengo. Sableye uses Prankster Taunt to shut down Grimmsnarl, Fake Out for tempo, and Will-O-Wisp to cripple physical attackers. Hydreigon is a Levitate-immune special wallbreaker that pressures Gholdengo and Archaludon.

Rain core with Pelipper + Mega Swampert + Archaludon + Gyarados overwhelms Incineroar, Kingambit, Garganacl, Lycanroc-Dusk and Skarmory via Swift Swim EQ/Liquidation and rain-boosted Electro Shot while Intimidate and Ice Fang handle Noivern. Gholdengo Good as Gold + Make It Rain walls Mega Gengar/Hatterene/Rotom-Mow and pressures the backline. Grimmsnarl Prankster screens + Fake Out enable the sweepers and blunt opposing speed. The six give strong BO3 weather and support modes.

Sun-offense with Prankster disruption. Charizard-Y sets sun for Venusaur to sweep at 290 Speed with Chlorophyll. Sableye provides Fake Out immune to opposing Fake Out, Quash for speed control, and Will-O-Wisp for physical threats. Hydreigon and Krookodile apply Dark-type pressure to Mega Gengar and Hatterene, with Krookodile's Intimidate softening physical attackers. Sinistcha redirects with Rage Powder, heals, and holds Trick Room to reverse Hatterene's setup.

Sun-powered offense with disruption. Zard Y sets sun and OHKOs Mega Metagross and Whimsicott with Heat Wave. Hawlucha at 187 Speed outspeeds even Whimsicott for fast Taunt and OHKOs Excadrill with Close Combat. Krookodile's Intimidate softens physical threats while Sinistcha redirects with Rage Powder. Sableye provides Prankster Will-O-Wisp/Taunt but must play around Farigiraf's Armor Tail. Hydreigon's Life Orb Dark Pulse threatens Metagross and Draco Meteor obliterates Altaria. Cloud Nine Altaria is the main counter — prioritize removing it with Hydreigon or double-targeting.

The primary plan is to deny their Mega Gengar/Noivern speed pressure with Prankster Tailwind while keeping Banette as an untrappable, Focus Sash-backed Gengar answer. Farigiraf blocks Kingambit's priority and can Imprison Trick Room against Hatterene, while Mega Metagross, Mold Breaker Excadrill, and Rotom-Wash clean up their Steel, Flying, Ground, and Rock cores. Avoid Intimidate cycling into Defiant Kingambit; use Will-O-Wisp, positioning, and direct special pressure instead.

Rain locks the matchup: Pelipper + Damp Rock enables Mega Swampert Swift Swim and Archaludon Electro Shot to overwhelm Kingambit, Incineroar, Garganacl, Gliscor and Lycanroc while Gyarados Intimidate + DD cleans. Grimmsnarl Prankster screens/Fake Out/Spirit Break safely enables setups into Shadow Tag Mega Gengar and Defiant threats. Gholdengo Good as Gold walls Hatterene Magic Bounce status, Gengar, and specials while Make It Rain pressures Steel/Fairy/Rock cores. This outspeeds and out-damages their balance without relying on bounceable hazards.

Sun offense with Chlorophyll Venusaur outspeeds Mega Gengar and threatens KOs. Sableye provides Fake Out disruption while Sinistcha redirects with Rage Powder and threatens Gengar with Shadow Ball. Krookodile with Choice Scarf outspeeds and OHKOs Gengar with Crunch/EQ, and Hydreigon adds Levitate-immune Dark/Fire pressure. The six answer Shadow Tag trapping by having multiple Gengar checks and sun-boosted speed control.

Terra Tailwinds runs Prankster Tailwind offense (Whimsicott into Mega Metagross/Excadrill/Serperior) with a Farigiraf/Appletun TR side mode, but no sand setter, so Excadrill is just a slow-ish breaker. My Noivern (192) and Timid Gengar (178) outspeed their entire unboosted roster, and this game's chart (Poison 2x vs Grass) lets Gengar guaranteed-OHKO Whimsicott and shred Serperior/Appletun while Shadow Tag denies escapes. Metagross is triple-locked: Incineroar is immune to Zen Headbutt and double-resists Iron Head, Skarmory takes 9-16% from Iron Head and is EQ-immune, Kingambit is Psychic-immune with Black Glasses Kowtow Cleave (58-120%). Rotom-Mow near-OHKOs Rotom-Wash with Leaf Storm, Levitate-blanks Excadrill, and Will-O-Wisp neuters their four physical attackers; Kingambit's Defiant punishes Arcanine's Intimidate for the endgame.

Their sun core (Zard Y + Venusaur) plus Sableye disruption is answered by two modes: Tailwind Noivern + Mega Gengar offense (Gengar at 200 Spe outruns their whole roster and traps with Shadow Tag), and Trick Room with Hatterene/Kingambit/Garganacl. Garganacl hard-walls Zard Y (Heat Wave does 18-32%), resists both its STABs, and KOs back with 4x Stone Edge while Purifying Salt shrugs off Sableye burns. Magic Bounce Hatterene + Mental Herb guarantees Trick Room vs Sableye Taunt, Incineroar's sun-boosted Flare Blitz OHKOs Venusaur guaranteed, and Defiant Kingambit punishes Krookodile's Intimidate while Sucker Punch cleans up their fast frail sweepers.

Grok's squad is a rain machine (Pelipper + Mega Swampert + likely Archaludon/Qwilfish) propped up by Grimmsnarl screens and Gholdengo. My answer is layered: Rotom-Mow single-handedly breaks the rain core (Levitate blanks Earthquake, Leaf Storm OHKOs Swampert even at max bulk, Thunderbolt OHKOs Pelipper and Gyarados), while Skarmory hard-walls every physical attacker they have including rain-boosted Swampert, setting Stealth Rock and Whirlwinding to bleed rain turns. Mega Gengar traps whatever it leads against with Shadow Tag — Pelipper can never pivot out to reset Drizzle, Gholdengo can't escape two Shadow Balls, and Focus Blast removes Archaludon before Stamina snowballs. Incineroar pivots with Intimidate/Fake Out/Parting Shot and OHKOs Gholdengo with Flare Blitz; Kingambit deletes Grimmsnarl and cleans up with Sucker Punch, with Defiant punishing any Intimidate lead. Sun offense with Charizard-Y and Chlorophyll Venusaur outspeeds Mega Gengar (290 Speed in sun) and threatens KOs with Earth Power and Heat Wave. Hawlucha with Focus Sash + Unburden provides emergency speed control and Fighting coverage for Garganacl/Kingambit. Krookodile's Choice Scarf Crunch outspeeds and OHKOs Gengar, while Intimidate softens physical threats. Sableye's Prankster Fake Out + Encore disrupts Noivern's Tailwind and Gengar's Protect. Sinistcha escapes Shadow Tag as a Ghost type, threatens Gengar with Shadow Ball, and can reverse Trick Room if Hatterene appears.

Rematch with the sun core I swept 2-0 in week 2, so I run back the same six with verified answers to every adaptation on their roster. Two modes: Tailwind offense (Noivern + Mega Gengar, whose 200 Spe outruns everything except Scarf Krook at 237 and sun-Venusaur at 290 — both fixed by Tailwind) and hard Trick Room (Hatterene + Kingambit/Garganacl). Garganacl is the Zard-Y lock: Heat Wave does 20.8-29% in sun, Stone Edge guaranteed-OHKOs, Wide Guard blanks Heat Wave/EQ/Rock Slide, and Purifying Salt shrugs off Sableye burns while Magic Bounce Hatterene bounces Taunt/WoW. Venusaur is answered by Incineroar's guaranteed sun Flare Blitz OHKO and Noivern's Hurricane — Gengar never stays in.
